OK I pared down the code and appear to have located the issue
Here is thebare bones  code with all the libraries I wish to have in my real app

One problem is adding the 'Rstem' package independently. This is not a problem to remove
The second is the 'sentiment' package which depends on tm and Rstem. If I remove it, the full app works (other than the aspects of the code I need it for)
I tried putting it at head of libraries loaded but that did not help with any deployment

So this appears to identify the exact problem but is there a satisfactory solution?

ui.R

# library(sentiment)
library(tm)
library(wordcloud)
library(httr) # this needs to be loaded after tm as other wise the content function is masked

library(rvest) 
library(rlist)
library(pipeR)
 library(rCharts)
 library(colorspace)

library(XML)
#library(Rstem)



shinyUI(fluidPage(

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(

  
    ),

   
    mainPanel(
      dataTableOutput("summaryTable")

      
    )
  )
  

))


server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  data <- reactive({
    
    initURL <- "http://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2014/jul/24/fifty-shades-of-grey-trailer-review"
    inithtml <- content(GET(initURL),"parsed")
   
    tag <-inithtml[xpath("//*/div[@id='d2-root']/@data-discussion-id")][[1]][1][[1]]
    commentURL <- paste0("http://discussion.theguardian.com/discussion/",tag,"?orderby=oldest&per_page=50&commentpage=1#show-all")
    html <- content(GET(commentURL), "parsed")
    
    words <- html[xpath('//*[contains(concat( " ", @class, " " ), concat( " ", "d2-body", " " ))]//text()')] %>>% 
      list.map(
           xmlValue(.,trim = TRUE) %>>% ## so need XML as well m piper The %>>% operator evaluates the function call on the right-hand side with the left-hand side object being the first argument
           strsplit("[^a-zA-Z]") %>>% 
           unlist(use.names = FALSE) %>>%  
           tolower %>>% 
           list.filter(nchar(.) > 3L)) %>>%
           unlist %>>%
           table %>>%
           list.sort(desc(.)
                     ) 
    
    
    df <- data.frame(words)

info=list(df=df)
print(df)
    return(info)
    
  })
  
  

output$summaryTable <- renderDataTable({
  tbl <- data()$df})





})
